atoms.a: Why Do We Use Fossil Fuels?
atoms.b: Fossil fuels can be burnt to generate electricity whenever it is needed. Some other methods, such as wind turbines and solar cells, can only work if the weather is right. Many of our existing power plants are designed to burn fossil fuels. The industry is currently profitable and provides many people with work.
Burning fossil fuels produces carbon dioxide, which contributes to global warming. It also creates other air pollution that has long-term effects on human health.
The methods used to extract fossil fuels from the ground cause damage to the environment. For example, areas of land are completely cleared to make room for coal mines.
Our planet only has a limited supply of fossil fuels.
